heading: INT. FUNERAL PARLOR - BACK ROOM - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. FUNERAL PARLOR - BACK ROOM - AFTERNOON
A narrow room behind the chapel, lined with folding chairs and a coffee urn.
Sun through frosted glass makes the floor look wet.
Chrysanthemums crowd a card table.
Through the wall comes the muffled sound of a hymn.
LEOPOLD VANCE, sixties, in a black suit that fits him like borrowed armor, pours coffee into two paper cups with great care.
His sister HESTER, early sixties, in a navy dress, sits very straight, hands folded over her purse.
Neither of them looks at the woman standing in the doorway.
A WOMAN, forties, in a plain gray coat, damp at the shoulders.
She holds a small wrapped box with both hands, as if it might spill.
Excuse me. I'm sorry. I didn't know where to go.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: The service is in the chapel.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: I know. I stood at the back. Then I left.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: You should have stayed.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: I didn't think I was welcome.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Leopold sets a cup in front of Hester and holds the other out toward the woman.
Coffee.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: She takes it.
Drinks.
Her hands tremble just slightly.
Thank you.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: You were his friend?
units.name: HESTER

units.text: For nineteen years.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Nineteen. He never mentioned you.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: No. He wouldn't have.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Why not?
units.name: HESTER

units.text: The woman looks at the box.
At the two of them.
At the hymn leaking through the wall.
My name is Adaeze. Adaeze Nwosu. He used to bring me flowers on Thursdays. Chrysanthemums.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Leopold glances at the card table.
At the flowers.
His hand tightens around the urn spout.
Those are his favorites.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: I know. He told me.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: Leo.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: It's all right, Hester.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: It is not all right. Who is this woman?
units.name: HESTER

units.text: I'm not here to take anything. I brought him something.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: She places the box on the table.
Hester doesn't touch it.
Leopold does, slowly, and peels back the paper.
Inside, a small clay bowl, hand-glazed, a crack mended in gold.
You made this.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: I'm a potter. He came to my studio the day his wife died. He sat for hours. I didn't know his name until the second week.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: Our brother was married to Lena for forty years.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Yes. And she died in March. And he came to me in April.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: Leopold lowers himself into a folding chair, the bowl in both hands.
He was lonely.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: He had us.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: He said that too. He said you were kind and you never asked him anything.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: Hester opens her mouth to answer and doesn't.
Outside, the hymn ends.
A pause, then the rustle of a congregation rising.
Will you sit with us for the burial, Adaeze?
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: If you'll have me.
units.name: ADAEZE

units.text: We will.
units.name: LEOPOLD

units.text: Hester stares at the bowl.
At the gold line through the clay.
Then she pulls out a handkerchief from her purse and, without a word, offers it to Adaeze.
